The bottleneck identified in Mem0 is not primarily related to storage but rather to the assembly (post-retrieval aggregation) process [2606.01435]. However, regarding the knowledge update in A-MEM, the mechanism ports from a max(serial) approach to a max(timestamp) one, but even with this change, it only ties the Long-Term Memory Reasoning (LLM) judgment performance with 57.8% vs 64.4%, based on a sample size of 45 [2606.01435].

Vector-based Memory Architecture (eMoT): The paper [2606.02054] introduces eMoT, which aims to address the limitations of standard models in multi-step reasoning tasks, particularly unconstrained hallucinations and poor numerical computation. The central design trade-off addressed by eMoT is the balance between evolving a Memory-of-Thought via symbolic anchoring and memory corrosion, ensuring that the model's long-term memory remains reliable and accurate over time.

The MemoryStore interface and fan-out router are key components of this architecture. The central design trade-off addressed by memorywire is the balance between flexibility in managing various types of memories and efficiency in executing memory operations.
